Who am I?

Strategy first.
Story always.


Most content fails because it speaks at people instead of understanding them first. I help brands uncover what their audience cares about and turn those insights into content that builds trust, engagement, and growth.

I'm Nidhi Agarwal, a content strategist at the intersection of data and editorial thinking — with a BBA, a Digital Marketing certification, and an MA in English Literature. I've always been curious about people—what they care about, what they struggle with, and why they choose to engage with certain content. That curiosity led me to content strategy.

Today, I help brands understand their audience and turn those insights into content that connects, builds trust, and drives results.

My background in literature helps me understand stories. My background in marketing helps me understand people. Together, they help me create content that is both meaningful and effective.

I'm particularly interested in content roles including Content Strategy, SEO and AI Content Management, Content Marketing, and Brand Storytelling.

A
SEO as the Foundation
Blog content that ranks creates compounding traffic. Every article is a long-term asset — not a post that disappears in 48 hours. I build content that earns traffic for months, not days.
B
Social as the Amplifier
Every blog becomes a carousel. Every audience question becomes a Reel. The comment section is free keyword research. Social doesn't exist separately — it feeds the system and drives traffic back.
C
Influencers as Distribution
Influencers amplify the right content to audiences SEO can't reach. At Affable.ai, I understood this ecosystem from the inside — writing content that educated the brands doing the briefing.
D
Content → Conversion
Every piece has a job in the funnel — awareness, consideration, or conversion. I map content to business outcomes, not just keywords. Traffic that arrives should do something valuable when it gets there.

Strategy Sample

Thinking applied to
a real brand.

A full content strategy analysis of Plum Goodness — gaps, audience blindspots, and three specific strategic recommendations.

Content Strategy Analysis · D2C Skincare · Plum Goodness
Where the strategy is working,
and where it isn't.
Blog · Instagram · SEO · Audience Research · Recommendations

"Plum has the brand presence to dominate the Indian skincare content space. What's holding them back is a strategy that reacts to trends instead of building a system — and content that talks about the brand instead of the audience."

Finding 1 — Topic Gap
Missing high-volume beginner searches: "how to start a skincare routine," "how to know your skin type." These are the highest-intent readers Plum isn't capturing.
Finding 2 — Audience Gap
Male skincare audience is almost completely unaddressed. Plum has the Phy sub-brand — the products exist. The content strategy hasn't caught up.
Finding 3 — System Gap
Blog and Instagram are completely disconnected operations. Neither feeds the other. A connected content pipeline would significantly increase the value of both.
Finding 4 — Engagement Gap
Instagram gets millions of views but engagement is low — the content stops the scroll but doesn't create connection. It's brand-centric when it should be audience-centric.
